text:
### Observed differences

- **The fixed order between two activity groups became mixed.** Earlier, in all 21 measured cross-pairs, a first-group activity (A15, A16, A17, A19, A20) preceded the second-group activity (A21–A25) in 100 in 100 traces, and each pair co-occurred in every trace. In the later window, co-occurrence is still 100 in 100, but the order is mixed: A21 now precedes A15, A16 or A17 in about 73–74 in 100 traces (before: never) and precedes A20 in about 94 in 100, while pairs with A19 keep the earlier order in about 54–79 in 100 and pairs such as A15–A23 or A17–A25 are close to even (about 52–57 vs 43–48). [REL001, REL005, REL009, REL013, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- **Cross-group step gaps shrank.** In the later window A20 is immediately followed by A23, A24 or A25 in about 48, 55 and 40 in 100 cases (before: never; gaps were 2–4 steps), and A15, A16 or A17 reach A21 in one step in about 33–46 in 100 cases (before: never); these gap shares rest on only 33–54 observed pairs per activity pair in the later window. Distances within the first group also spread out (A15 to A17 one step apart in about 70 in 100 cases before versus 34 in 100 after). [LAG003, LAG005, LAG012, LAG019, LAG029, LAG030, LAG031]
- **Event positions of the two groups moved towards each other.** A20's mean relative position rose from about 0.61 to 0.71 of the trace and A15/A16/A17 from about 0.56 to 0.62, while A21 fell from about 0.64 to 0.55 and A23–A25 from about 0.69 to 0.63; positional spread increased for all ten activities. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- **New transitions in both directions between the groups.** In the later window A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 send roughly three to five in ten of their observed outgoing transitions to A21–A25 (before: none observed), and A21–A25 send roughly three to five in ten back to A15–A20 (before: none observed). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]
- **Accompanying edge changes.** A20's observed outgoing transitions, previously all to A21, now go to A31 in about 48 in 100 cases and to A21 in only about 7 in 100; A30 now leads to A21 in about 46 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before: only A19); A22 reaches A31 in one step in about 56 in 100 cases (before: always). [DIR005, DIR007, DIR011, LAG036, LAG051]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the strict sequencing between the two activity groups was relaxed into a largely mixed order: A21, A22, A23, A24 and A25, which in the earlier window always executed after A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20, now frequently execute before them, while both groups still occur together in essentially every trace, so participation itself did not change. [REL001, REL005, REL009, REL013, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]

The relational evidence shows this directly and consistently: every one of the 21 cross-pairs moved from a 100-in-100 fixed order to mixed orders (about 7 to 79 in 100 still first-group-first) with co-occurrence unchanged at 100 in 100 in both windows, and the new cross-group transitions, the converging event positions and the shorter cross-group gaps all point the same way; each item's difference also exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits. The screening comparison rules out chance as an explanation for the ensemble: 93 items qualified against roughly 0.72 expected by chance across 145 tested units. [REL001, REL013, REL017, REL019, DIR001, DIR006, POS005, POS006, LAG029, LAG030]

An important competing explanation remains: the later window could mix several case variants, each with its own fixed order, rather than truly interleaving the groups within individual cases; the widely differing order shares across pairs (about 7 to 79 in 100) fit mixing but do not rule this out. POS and LAG use event positions rather than clock time, so no claim about timing is made. [REL001, REL013, REL017, REL019]

Other differences: A20 now hands over mainly to A31 instead of to A21, A30 can hand over to A21, and A31 is reached later from A23 and A25 than before; these entry and tail changes accompany the reordering but are not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR005, DIR011, LAG040, LAG047]
